items.title: Gallagher sees buyers increasing limits as property rates fall
items.original_title: Gallagher sees buyers increasing limits as property rates fall
items.rss_title: Gallagher sees buyers increasing limits as property rates fall
items.rss_description: Commercial insurance buyers are using savings from falling property rates to restore coverage and increase limits, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.’s top executive said Thursday, as the brokerage reported an 18.2% increase in third-quarter revenue.
items.extracted_text: Patrick Gallagher Jr. Agents and Brokers , Cyber Risks , D&O , Excess and Surplus Lines , Financial Results , General liability , Mergers and Acquisitions , Property Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. , AssuredPartners Oct 29, 2026 Commercial insurance buyers are using savings from falling property rates to restore coverage and increase limits, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.’s top executive said Thursday, as the brokerage reported an 18.2% increase in third-quarter revenue. “As property pricing eases, clients are opting in and using the savings to buy back coverage, increase limits or improve structure after several years of opting out,” Chairman and CEO J. Patrick Gallagher Jr. said on an earnings call with analysts. The current insurance rating environment is contributing about 1 percentage point to organic revenue growth, while new business, strong client retention and positive exposure growth helped drive 5% organic growth in the brokerage segment in the quarter, Mr. Gallagher said. “Rates are just one part of the equation,” he said. Global property insurance renewal premiums fell 6% in the third quarter, compared with a 10% decline in the second quarter, reflecting the mix and seasonality of renewals rather than a change in the underlying market, Mr. Gallagher said. Casualty renewal premiums increased 4% overall, including general liability, commercial auto and umbrella. Professional lines, including directors and officers liability and cyber, rose 2%, while workers compensation increased 1%. Excluding property, renewal premiums increased 3%, with larger increases in the U.S. than in international markets, Mr. Gallagher said. U.S. excess and surplus lines property insurance remained highly competitive, particularly for catastrophe-exposed risks, he said. Gallagher reported third-quarter revenue of $3.93 billion, driven by its acquisition of AssuredPartners and 5% organic growth. Its core brokerage segment generated $3.5 billion in revenue, up 18.9%, including 5% organic growth, while its risk management segment, which includes third-party administrator Gallagher Bassett Services, reported $457 million in revenue, up 13.7%, including 10% organic growth. More than a year after completing its acquisition of AssuredPartners, client retention at the acquired brokerage remains strong, Mr. Gallagher said. Gallagher closed five acquisitions during the quarter, with estimated annualized revenue of about $102 million, compared with six acquisitions accounting for about $3.04 billion in estimated annualized revenue in the prior-year quarter. Brokerage acquisition activity is slowing, and acquisition multiples have declined, but Gallagher has more than 30 term sheets signed or in preparation, representing about $300 million in annualized revenue, Mr. Gallagher said. The company reported net earnings of $406 million, up 48.4% from $273.6 million a year earlier, as brokerage segment earnings rose 26%. EBITDAC increased 29% to $1.05 billion. Recall that the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF (ticker ILS), was launched and listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) ARCA platform in early April , becoming the first catastrophe bond fund strategy to be US exchange-listed and traded. Then in late August, we learned that Brookmont Capital Management would be moving the cat bond ETF strategy to the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) which officially transitioned on September 18th, 2026. As we explained at the time, the key drive behind this move was to expand market maker participation in the catastrophe bond fund, which proved to be a challenge when fund was first launched. Brookmont explained that since its inception, the fund has managed to attract steady investor interest supported by an active secondary market. In addition, Brookmont also announced that financial technology firm GTS is now the lead market maker for the catastrophe bond fund. The company emphasised that joining forces with GTS and transferring to the TXSE will strengthen the fund’s trading structure and drive its next phase of growth. We reported back in August that the Brookmont Catastrophic Bond ETF had reached $95.6 million in AUM, but as mentioned, the fund has now managed to surpass an impressive $150 million. Brookmont also confirmed that the fund will continue to trade under the ticker ILS, while its name, investment objectives, and investment strategies will all remain unchanged. Ethan Powell, Principal and Chief Investment Officer of Brookmont Capital Management, commented: “Working with GTS and moving ILS to TXSE mark an important next chapter in the continued growth of the fund. The response to ILS since launch has reinforced our conviction that there is a place for catastrophe bonds in a broad range of portfolios, and we’re excited to continue expanding access to the asset class.” Rob Marrocco, Global Head of Exchange-Traded Products for TXSE, said: “The future of the ETF ecosystem is going to be dictated by quality and innovation, and that is exactly what Brookmont has been focused on for ILS and now their partnership with GTS and the Texas Stock Exchange. items.extracted_text: EPA Response to 2023 Ohio Train Derailment Will be Investigated Article 0 Comments The Environmental Protection Agency’s response to the disastrous 2023 East Palestine train derailment will be investigated after local residents of the small town on the Ohio-Pennsylvania border and Vice President JD Vance pressed for the review. The Inspector General of the EPA announced the investigation Tuesday to assess the agency’s response to the worst rail disaster in more than a decade and the subsequent health and environmental concerns that have developed despite the EPA’s assurances to the public that no toxic levels of chemicals lingered in the community weeks and months later. An assortment of chemicals spilled and caught fire after the failed bearing sent the Norfolk Southern train careening off the tracks late one Friday night in February 2023. Residents evacuated as officials decided three days later to blow open five rail cars and burn the vinyl chloride inside. The National Transportation Safety Board determined the “vent and burn” move that generated a massive black plume of smoke and sent chemicals drifting across several states was unnecessary. But at the time, the officials in charge of the emergency response worried the tank cars might explode and do even more harm. Jami Wallace and other East Palestine residents have been pushing for this investigation — much like they pressed the EPA initially to test for whether cancer-causing dioxins were released in their hometown — so she said “I’m going to cry” when she heard the news. Since the derailment, Wallace has kept track of more than 80 people who live in the area and have developed cancer, although it’s difficult to prove that every illness is directly linked to the derailment. “It’s like we’ve had to push them along the way for every single thing they did, and then they didn’t even do it right,” said Wallace, who promised never to give up the fight. “We’re not going to stop when you poison our kids.” The recent request from Vance and the head of the EPA helped get the investigation started. But multiple complaints from residents and whistleblowers have also been made in the years since the derailment. The Inspector General’s office said this investigation will determine whether the EPA fulfilled its responsibilities and whether the EPA had “sufficient data to support the agency’s public communications” assuring residents they were safe to return home and live in the small town. Testing experts questioned whether the test data EPA shared with the public obscured the risks and whether the agency could determine just how dangerous it is to be exposed to this cocktail of chemicals. Health standards are generally based only on exposure to a single chemical. Wallace said she’s not sure how much good might come out of this investigation, but it will continue to put a bit of light on the lingering concerns around East Palestine. “If nothing else, at least we’re getting attention again,” Wallace said. “And people know that we’re here and that we are not OK.” Norfolk Southern agreed to a $600 million class action settlement with residents, but that money has been largely tied up in the courts and questions about the initial settlement administrator mishandling the funds. A group of residents has also sued because they argue the class action attorneys misled them and pressured them into signing the deal. A separate federal settlement that includes a $15 million fine for the railroad and $55 million to pay for decades of medical exams and groundwater testing has been under review for more than two years without a judge approving it. Norfolk Southern is seeking to merge with Union Pacific and create the nation’s first transcontinental railroad. But that $85 billion deal still faces an extensive review by the Surface Transportation Board. Photo: FILE – A black plume rises over East Palestine, Ohio, as a result of a controlled detonation of a portion of the derailed Norfolk Southern trains, Feb. 6, 2023. West Virginia’s water utility says it’s taking precautionary steps following the derailment of a train hauling chemicals that later sent up a toxic plume in Ohio. The utility said in a statement on Sunday, Feb. 16, 2023 that it has enhanced its treatment processes even though there hasn’t been a change in raw water at its Ohio River intake. (AP Photo/Gene J. items.title: AI use should focus on better decisions, not efficiency: panelists
items.original_title: AI use should focus on better decisions, not efficiency: panelists
items.rss_title: AI use should focus on better decisions, not efficiency: panelists
items.rss_description: When adopting artificial intelligence, builders and their insurers should shift their sights from achieving efficiency to improving decisions and reducing risk, said panelists at the International Risk Management and Insurance Construction Risk Conference.
items.extracted_text: “If I have a 10% reduction in expense, that doesn’t hold a candle to a one-point basis reduction in loss ratio,” said Jay Bell, chief operating officer at Zurich North America. “It’s not even close. But the majority of the focus is still on efficiency.” AI can help identify unexpected risks during preconstruction or underwriting, and by monitoring projects, Mr. Bell said. “I’m mostly interested in engaging with vendors who can help me, through a partnership with the insurer and contractor, to identify those signals that we believe have the highest probability to turn into a claim. If we can prevent one person from dying, it’s successful.” The growth in construction today is dominated by large, complex projects, such as data centers, advanced manufacturing, and power generation, said Michelle Sartain, president of Marsh Risk U.S. and Canada, in a general session address. In the face of “more significant” and “more interconnected” risks, AI can help builders improve planning, monitor project progress and “recognize emerging challenges early,” Ms. Sartain said. By making efficiency the main use case for implementing AI, managers virtually guarantee layoffs because shedding workers is the most common way to recognize the savings achieved through efficiency, Mr. Bell said. Instead, AI should “empower people” to improve outcomes. Cheri Hanes, head of construction innovation and sustainability at Axa XL, gave examples of how builders can use AI to improve work quality. An engineer reviewing five subcontractor materials estimates a day could use AI to “fact-check” their findings, reducing costly errors. That would be preferable to having the AI review 10 estimates a day and the engineer acting as fact-checker, Ms. Hanes said. “We’ve already established that the human can’t thoroughly look at 10 of them a day, right?” Ms. Hanes said. “So now the human is just not just getting used by the machine, it’s getting used up by the machine. They’re not going to be happy. They know they’re not producing their best work.” AI can also be a “second pair of eyes” in safety reviews, said Ms. Hanes, who is based in Dallas. An AI chatbot reviewing a photo of a jobsite can do “a not so bad job” at identifying hazards, she said. They’re even better when connected to data from the Occupational Safety and Health Administration or a company manual, she said. AI implementation and benefits are likely to vary based in part on firm size, said Hugh Seaton, Austin-based managing director of consultancy AI Edge. Smaller firms may rely on chatbots and assistants, while larger firms will integrate AI with their existing systems. The largest and most sophisticated firms will build their own AI systems. These firms will be “light years ahead” of competitors because “you can make the expertise of the company available to anybody who is subject to permission,” resulting in “better decisions, better estimates, faster understanding of a problem,” Mr. Seaton said. These firms will need a strong, dedicated internal technology team. Improving data quality and structure is key to ensuring that AI can synthesize data throughout the company and produce the best outputs, panelists said. As AI advances, hallucinations — in which AI fabricates an answer — have become rare, said Mr. Bell, who is based in West Simsbury, Connecticut. Instead, AI may be producing a wrong answer because the query lacks the proper context, or because the bot is reviewing contradictory information held in a company’s knowledge repository. He said Zurich is currently reviewing and restructuring its SharePoint files to improve the reliability of AI answers sourced from them. items.title: Markel enters into reinsurance agreement with Enstar unit
items.original_title: Markel enters into reinsurance agreement with Enstar unit
items.rss_title: Markel enters into reinsurance agreement with Enstar unit
items.rss_description: Markel Insurance, the insurance operations within Markel Group Inc., said Thursday that it has entered into a multi-billion-dollar adverse development cover reinsurance agreement covering Markel’s run-off global reinsurance business and certain exited lines within its insurance operations.
items.extracted_text: The reinsurance agreement with Enstar Group’s wholly owned subsidiary, Cavello Bay Reinsurance, includes reserves of $4.8 billion, of which Markel will retain the first $2.6 billion and retrocede the next $2.3 billion to Enstar, Markel said in a statement. Markel will pay Enstar a risk premium of $120 million and obtain adverse loss development coverage of $1.2 billion above the $4.8 billion of subject reserves under the transaction terms, the statement said. The reserves involved in the deal include 2025 and prior underwriting years of business written within Markel’s Global Reinsurance division as well as its exited risk managed professional liability, architects and engineers and other run-off lines within its global insurance operations. Markel will retain claims control over the involved portfolio, according to the statement. The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of fourth-quarter 2026. “This transaction provides additional certainty as these liabilities continue to run off and allows us to continue our focus on growing our core specialty insurance business,” Simon Wilson, CEO of Markel Insurance, said in the statement. In a separate statement from Enstar, CEO Dominic Silvester said: “The agreement will give Markel greater certainty over its legacy liabilities as it focuses on growing its core specialty insurance business.” Related News The BI Top 10 for the week of Oct. 26, 2026 October 30, 2026 Bayer wins Roundup weedkiller cancer trial while awaiting settlement ruling October 30, 2026 Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance October 30, 2026 Gallagher sees buyers increasing limits as property rates fall October 29, 2026 Ryan Specialty posts 4% organic growth for third quarter October 29, 2026 AI use should focus on better decisions, not efficiency: panelists October 29, 2026 EverPeak names Daley chief underwriting officer October 29, 2026 Greek PM calls for global maritime truce after Greek ship sunk in drone attack October 29, 2026 Liberty Mutual needn’t defend highway builders in pileup: court October 29, 2026

items.extracted_text: Cat bond risk spreads may decrease 10% in 2027, but market healthy and growing: Plenum - Artemis.bm Cat bond risk spreads may decrease 10% in 2027, but market healthy and growing: Plenum - Artemis.bm Cat bond risk spreads may decrease 10% in 2027, but market healthy and growing: Plenum 30th October 2026 - Author: Jack Willard Speaking during a recent webinar, executives at Plenum Investments AG outlined that while catastrophe bond risk spreads have tightened around 15% and are expected to decrease around 10% in 2027, cat bonds remain a healthy and very diversifying and attractive asset class. Plenum Investments recently hosted a webinar, where key executives from the firm analysed the current state of the catastrophe bond market and provided an overview of this year’s Atlantic hurricane season. During the webinar, Henrik Hopmann, Junior Portfolio Manager at the firm, shared how Plenum expects the cat bond market’s momentum to continue as we begin to move towards year-end. “We still see a continuously expanding market, a very healthy growing market. There’s still a lot of demand for cat bonds in the market, and we expect the market to grow and surpass the $70 billion mark at the end of this quarter,” Hopmann explained. “Noteworthy is the high number of new sponsors that come to market and have been coming to the market year-to-date. We expect even more to come in this quarter with the issuances that are ongoing at the moment.” As the pipeline for cat bond issuance continues to build for the fourth-quarter of 2026, Artemis is tracking what will mark only the second ever year where issuance of catastrophe bonds will exceed the $20 billion level . Regarding risk spreads, Hopmann noted the cat bond market is currently in a softening phase. Spreads have tightened around 15% compared to last year, driven in part by the end of the hurricane season without any losses. Looking ahead, Plenum said spreads may decline 10% in 2027, although this is obviously dependent on any loss activity as well as any other capital markets effects that could occur. Hopmann added: “Worthwhile to mention is that this spread development is not uniform across all segments of the cat bond market. We see this spread development also differentiating between different segments of the cat bond market very differently. “There has been a huge spread decrease as spreads have come down quite significantly in California wildfire but still remain at very high levels. But we also see segments in the market where spreads are increasing, which highlights again the need for selectivity within the market.” Attention then turned towards this year’s Atlantic hurricane season, as David Strasser, Senior Portfolio Manager responsible for risk modelling, noted that this year’s season has been the quietest on record based on hurricane counts and Accumulated Cyclone Energy (ACE) levels. Strasser also underscored how El Niño was one of the key drivers, for why this year’s hurricane season was so quiet in the Atlantic. Data from Plenum also showcased how El Niño is going to continue to intensify over the next several weeks, reaching its peak around December. Strasser also said El Niño is expected to dissipate by April 2027, when conditions are forecast to return to ENSO-neutral. He said conditions may remain strong however until around February or March 2027. “Even though it’s quite early to make a precise forecast, but we can already say that there is a very good chance that the hurricane season next year is going to be more active than what we have seen this year because by the time El Niño will have dissipated,” Strasser added. “As I mentioned, the peak of El Niño is expected this December, during the winter, and then the question arises as to what could the potential impact be on the cat bond market from this very strong El Niño? The question is ‘Is the riskiness of the cat bond market going to increase or not?’ And the short answer to this question is, we don’t expect the risk in the cat bond market to increase or to change based on this very strong El Niño.” Strasser explained that Plenum’s reasoning behind this is because the so-called peril-regions that are affected by this very strong El Niño are largely not covered by the cat bond market. As a prime example, Strasser outlined that El Niño could bring coastal flooding and heavy rainfall to California but importantly explained that California flood risk is not meaningfully covered by the cat bond market. He also noted that wildfire risk in California, which is covered by the cat bond market, could potentially decrease because of the expected wetter conditions that El Niño is expected to bring to the state. Concluding the webinar, Dirk Schmelzer, Head Portfolio Manager ILS/CAT Bonds and Partner at Plenum, reaffirmed confidence in the asset class. “We’ve seen that we are currently in a very healthy market. Spreads have come down, but are expected to stay around 5%, so a little bit lower than last year throughout the upcoming 12-month period,” Schmelzer said. “We maintain a very selective underwriting approach. I think you can clearly see this in the differences, especially to a market weight portfolio on some of the peril regions or structures that we try to underweight significantly. We do not take significant overweight’s in certain peril regions, at least compared to the historical stress tests. There is no single region where we would take more risk because of lowering the risk in other regions. But especially for the dynamic strategy, we maintain a very balanced exposure to the overall cat bond market.” Concluding: “Cat bonds remain a very diversifying and attractive asset class. Even with spreads being slightly lower than in prior years, and performance coming down with that. items.extracted_text: SafePoint more than doubles Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond target to $600m - Artemis.bm SafePoint more than doubles Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond target to $600m - Artemis.bm SafePoint more than doubles Nature Coast Re 2026-2 cat bond target to $600m 30th October 2026 - Author: Steve Evans SafePoint Insurance Company is now seeking its largest catastrophe bond sponsorship ever, as the expansive insurance platform has more than doubled the target size to $600 million for its new Nature Coast Re Ltd. (Series 2026-2) cat bond issuance, we are told. SafePoint returned earlier this month with an initial target to secure $250 million of multi-year named storm reinsurance protection from its latest foray into the cat bond market. Now, we understand that SafePoint is targeting a significant upsizing for this offering, more than doubling it to provide as much as $600 million of multi-year reinsurance protection. At the same time, we understand the price guidance for each of the two tranches of notes on offer has been lowered. This will become SafePoint’s sixth cat bond under the Nature Coast Re special purpose insurer, and its tenth cat bond sponsorship in total. Read about all of SafePoint’s cat bonds in our extensive Deal Directory . SafePoint’s largest cat bond sponsorship prior to this one was its $250 million Nature Coast Re Ltd. (Series 2026-1) issuance that came to market in February this year. As a result, this now $600 million target for the 2026-2 offering is meaningfully larger, demonstrating SafePoint’s appetite for efficient reinsurance protection, as well as its growing stature as an underwriting company and platform. We won’t repeat all the details of the cat bond in our updates on size and pricing, so be sure to visit the Deal Directory entry for more background on the transaction . Nature Coast Re Ltd. is offering investors two tranches of Series 2026-2 catastrophe bond notes to source reinsurance for SafePoint Insurance Company itself and the two reciprocal exchanges it operates, to cover losses from named storms on an indemnity and per-occurrence trigger basis, while the protection will run across a four-year period from December 1st. Initially the target was for $250 million of reinsurance across the two tranches, which has now been more than doubled to $600 million, as we said. In our earlier report on this deal when it launched , we explained that the cat bond will cover losses in the widest range of US states of any cat bond in SafePoint’s history, as the insurer continues to expand and grow into new locations. What was a $100 million tranche of Series 2026-2 Class AA notes are now targeted at $300 million in size, sources said. The Class AA notes come with an initial base expected loss of 0.73% and were initially offered to investors with price guidance in a range for a spread of between 4% and 4.75%, but that range has now been lowered to between 3.75% and 4%, we understand. What was a $150 million tranche of Series 2026-2 Class A notes are now also targeted to be $300 million in size. The Class A notes have an initial base expected loss of 1.66% and were first offered to investors with price guidance in a range for a spread of between 6.75% to 7.5%, but again we’re told this has been lowered to a revised range of 6.25% to 6.75%. SafePoint looks set to benefit from catastrophe bond market conditions, in being able to secure much more reinsurance than initially sought, with the pricing now targeted at the bottom-end of or lower than the initially marketed ranges. A $600 million catastrophe bond will be a notable increase to SafePoint’s protection from the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market if secured and this could be another deal that sends a strong signal to potential cat bond sponsors about the currently attractive issuance conditions in the market. items.rss_title: Toast Sued by FTC For Misleading Customers on Subscriptions

items.extracted_text: Toast Sued by FTC For Misleading Customers on Subscriptions Article 0 Comments The U.S. Federal Trade Commission and a group of eight states sued Toast Inc., alleging the restaurant management and financial technology company falsely told customers they could try its products for free before enrolling them in a subscription that was difficult to cancel. Toast, which had 156,000 customers and $6.1 billion in revenue last year, violated federal and state consumer protection laws, according to the suit filed Thursday in California federal court. The company bills itself as a “one-stop shop” for restaurants, helping manage inventory, take orders and accept payments. In a statement, Toast said it will fight the suit, arguing the FTC improperly used a 2010 law governing certain online subscription practices to target the company’s commercial agreements with restaurant customers. “No court has held that” the Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act “applies to negotiated business-to-business agreements, and we don’t believe it applies here,” Toast said. The company had claimed it offered 24/7 customer support, but instead provided minimal customer service, the FTC alleged. Toast also began charging a 99-cent order-processing fee to consumers that placed digital orders above $10 in 2023, in addition to the payment processing fees paid by the restaurant, without clearly disclosing that money would be paid to the company and not the restaurant, according to the complaint. The FTC also alleged that Toast made it difficult for restaurants and small businesses to cancel their subscriptions, requiring at least 30 days notice and not offering an online cancellation option. The complaint also alleges Toast violated ROSCA, which requires companies to clearly and conspicuously disclose all material terms before charging consumers on an ongoing basis. items.rss_title: South Korean Court Rejects Tesla Owners’ Lawsuit Seeking ‘Full Self-Driving’ Refunds
items.rss_description: A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by dozens of Tesla owners seeking full refunds for money paid for “Full Self-Driving” driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. The Seoul Central District Court …
items.extracted_text: South Korean Court Rejects Tesla Owners’ Lawsuit Seeking ‘Full Self-Driving’ Refunds Article 0 Comments A South Korean court on Thursday rejected a lawsuit by dozens of Tesla owners seeking full refunds for money paid for “Full Self-Driving” driver-assistance software, ruling that the automaker had not breached its contractual obligations. The Seoul Central District Court ruled against the 88 plaintiffs, finding that the FSD option did not promise fully autonomous driving without human intervention and that Tesla had already provided some of the functions included in the package. The court said Tesla’s obligation to deliver additional features depended on technological advances and regulatory approvals, adding that buyers had been aware that some functions could take considerable time to become available. It also found that Tesla had provided basic Autopilot and Enhanced Autopilot functions, while a recent software update had added traffic light and sign recognition, as well as city-driving capabilities, to older vehicles equipped with Hardware 3 (HW3) computers. The ruling comes as the automaker faces similar legal challenges in other countries over delays in delivering self-driving capabilities long promised by CEO Elon Musk. Tesla did not immediately comment on the decision. In the lawsuit filed in 2024, the owners said: “Tesla Korea has been unable to implement the FSD system option in South Korea for more than eight years since it began selling it around March 2017.” The plaintiffs argued that Tesla had failed to deliver the promised technology, but the court rejected their interpretation of FSD as a system capable of fully autonomous driving, known as Level 5 automation. It also ruled that even if there had been delays in delivering some features, Tesla could not be held responsible for delays caused by compliance with domestic and overseas regulations. In China, 10 Tesla car owners have filed a joint lawsuit demanding refunds for FSD and seeking damages equal to three times the purchase price of the FSD option or the entire vehicle, according to a report. In the United States, a federal appeals court earlier this month blocked California Tesla owners from pursuing class action claims alleging the automaker misled buyers about its Full Self-Driving technology, although the underlying lawsuit remains pending. Musk has repeatedly predicted that Tesla would achieve fully autonomous driving, but that level of autonomy has not yet been delivered. items.extracted_text: AM Best Upgrades Credit Ratings of Kansas’ Upland Mutual Article 0 Comments AM Best has upgraded the Financial Strength Rating to A- (Excellent) from B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating to “a-” (Excellent) from “bbb+” (Good) of Upland Mutual Insurance, Inc. based in Junction City, Kansas. The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) has been revised to stable from positive. The ratings reflect Upland’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). The rating upgrades and revised outlooks to stable from positive reflect the consistent positive policyholder surplus growth over the latest five-year period. The rating upgrades also reflect the overall balance sheet assessment of very strong. Additionally, the rating upgrades recognize Upland’s sustained policyholders surplus growth over the past five years, generated from positive pre-tax operating performance supporting the strongest assessment of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Also, policyholder appreciation continued through Sept. 30, 2026. The rating upgrades also reflect Upland’s favorable net underwriting leverage conservative investment portfolio of fixed income investment that generated consistent net investment income favorable loss reserve development trends on a calendar and accident year basis and strong reinsurance program that protects its balance sheet from tail risk including catastrophe limits that cover a potential 1-in-1,000-year event at the 99.8% VaR. Additionally, Upland eliminated its overall financial leverage by repaying its outstanding balance of Federal Home Loan Bank borrowings. AM Best assesses Upland’s operating performance as adequate as its five-year average return on revenue and equity, combined ratio and operating ratio, compare favorably with the personal property composite. The limited business profile reflects Upland’s long-standing market presence in Kansas and distribution network of independent agents. The appropriate ERM assessment reflects Upland’s formalized risk appetite and tolerance statements maintained for key areas, aided by the company’s comprehensive reinsurance program. items.extracted_text: Hippo Continues to Diversify Portfolio in Q3 With Casualty, Commercial Article 0 Comments Insurtech Hippo posted net income for the third quarter 2026 of $9 million compared with about $98 million for the period a year ago. The San Jose, California-based insurer said the drop in net income was due to a $91 million gain the company booked after the sale of its homebuilder distribution network to The Baldwin Group, which closed Q3 2025. Gross written premium of $498 million for the third quarter increased 60% year over year to nearly $500 million. Hippo said all lines of business delivered growth, led by casualty and commercial multiperil lines which were up 146% and 63%, respectively, over Q3 2025. “The overall growth strategy is focused on improving underwriting profitability and reducing volatility, including through greater portfolio diversification,” Hippo said in a statement. “This growth did not come at the expense of underwriting discipline,” Hippo President and CEO Rick McCathron added during an earnings call with analysts. Net premiums written of $149 million increased 26% from Q3 2025. The combined ratio for Q3 was 98.4 versus 99.6 during the same period last year. McCathron said Hippo’s year-to-date combined ratio improved 20 points to 97.9 compared to last year. The CEO of the managing general agency said the “MGA market remains one of the fastest-growing and most innovative sectors of insurance. This market now generates gross premium of over $125 billion in the U.S., growing at 15% annually since 2019. “I am proud that Hippo is one of the leading program carriers supporting this growth and innovation.” Hippo’s AI initiatives includes claims management platform CLARA Analytics, which is showing a success rate in 9 of 10 first notice of losses, McCathron said. “This technology provides our claims operations the bandwidth to keep growing profitably. We continue to refine our underwriting and technology integrations and see a lot of runway ahead for our homeowners business,” he added. Topics Commercial Lines Casualty Was this article valuable? items.original_title: Trump to End Restrictions on Methane From Oil and Gas Drilling
items.rss_title: Trump to End Restrictions on Methane From Oil and Gas Drilling
items.rss_description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is “terminating” a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling. Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save companies …
items.extracted_text: Trump to End Restrictions on Methane From Oil and Gas Drilling Article 0 Comments President Donald Trump said Tuesday that his administration is “terminating” a Biden-era rule that aimed to cut planet-warming emissions of methane from oil and gas drilling. Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save companies and consumers billions of dollars and unlock 210 million barrels of oil. That’s equivalent to about 10 days of U.S. petroleum consumption. The move aims to encourage more domestic drilling as Trump faces criticism over high fuel prices amid the war in Iran . Methane is responsible for about a third of planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions, scientists estimate. Cuts in methane emissions have emerged in recent years as a global priority to slow the rate of climate change. Oil and gas operations are the largest industrial source of methane, which is the main component in natural gas and far more potent to the atmosphere than carbon dioxide in the short term. The invisible gas leaks from equipment and is released into the atmosphere or burned off as a waste product by oil drillers. Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin previewed the changes last month, saying they would eliminate the agency’s “Super Emitter Program” that requires companies to investigate and repair major methane releases from oil and natural gas facilities. The agency would also set less restrictive standards for small oil and gas wells. Trump said during Tuesday’s rally in Lubbock for Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton that Biden’s plan “crushed the small operators” with crippling regulations. “I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion in costs,” Trump said. The loosening of the emissions rule comes as Trump and Republicans in Congress have been methodically dismantling climate policies enacted under former President Joe Biden. That’s included the revocation of a scientific finding that was central to U.S. action on greenhouse gas emissions, lower fuel economy standards for vehicles and a move to repeal emission restrictions for coal and natural gas power plants . Environmental groups said the latest rollback will let companies continue polluting the atmosphere with gas that could be captured and provide energy to millions of households. Environmental Defense Fund President Fred Krupp said it gives a “free pass” to companies at the expense of American consumers. “EPA should be fighting this waste, not making it easier,” he said. Zeldin has said the methane rule would have cost $18 billion and was holding back the U.S. energy industry. The Biden methane rule was announced by officials including former Vice President Kamala Harris during a 2023 U.N. climate conference in the United Arab Emirates. Federal officials under Biden said it would prevent an estimated 58 million tons (52.6 million metric tonnes) of methane emissions by 2038 and reduce other pollutants that cause health problems. By 2034, the rule was projected to yield $98 billion in benefits. That figure was derived by calculating the future “social costs” of greenhouse gas emissions on public health and the environment, an approach rejected by Trump’s EPA. While previous regulations focused only on new oil and gas wells in the U.S., the Biden rule regulated existing wells. Operators also would have needed to plug leaking methane from smaller wells that produce just 6% of the nation’s oil and gas while accounting for up to half of all methane emissions from oil and gas fields. The final rule was published in 2024 . The EPA last year imposed an 18-month delay to give companies time to meet new inspection requirements and other provisions. The rule was crafted to be coordinated with a methane fee , approved in the 2022 climate law . The fee program would have levied a “waste emissions charge” of as much as $1,500 per metric ton of methane on energy producers that exceed a certain level of methane emissions. The fee marked the first time the U.S. government directly imposed a fee, or tax, on greenhouse gas emissions. Congress repealed it weeks after Trump took office. Officials also tried to rein in methane from oil and gas under former President Barack Obama, but that effort was scaled back during Trump’s first term. ___ Gruver reported from Fort Collins, Colorado. items.extracted_text: GM Paying $220 Million to Settle Allegations It Violated Driver Privacy Article 0 Comments General Motors will pay $220 million to settle allegations that it illegally sold drivers’ private behavior and location data to brokers, who then sold the information to insurers that used it to set and sometimes increase rates. The settlement, announced on Thursday, resolves claims by the attorneys general of 35 U.S. states and the District of Columbia over the automaker’s Smart Driver program, which enrolled millions of drivers between 2016 and its discontinuation in 2024. Other regulators have also reviewed GM’s handling of driver data. GM was accused of pitching Smart Driver to help people improve their personal driving safety, only to violate drivers’ privacy by reneging on its promise not to sell their data without permission. Many people who signed up were also enrolled in GM’s OnStar safety, navigation and diagnostic service. “People bought a car, not a tracking device,” Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield said in a statement. Rayfield’s office and the office of Washington Attorney General Nick Brown led the bipartisan state coalition. The settlement also requires GM to limit driving data it collects, and obtain drivers’ express consent before collecting or sharing that data. A GM spokesperson said the settlement reinforces other steps the Detroit automaker has taken to strengthen privacy. “Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share,” the spokesperson said. Insurers such as Allstate, Progressive and Berkshire Hathaway’s Geico use so-called telematics in monitoring drivers’ habits. They say the technology rewards good driving through lower premiums. The settlement follows GM’s agreement in May to pay $12.75 million to settle a California investigation into its alleged sale of driver data to two data brokers. items.extracted_text: Barclays Turns to Insurers to Hedge Billions of Data Center Debt Article 0 Comments Barclays Plc is looking to buy default protection on more than $10 billion of debt to finance artificial intelligence infrastructure in a bid to create capacity for more lending as hyperscaler funding needs soar. The London-based lender has been assessing the appetite among insurers in recent weeks to provide credit risk cover for the loans, according to people familiar with the matter. The talks are exploratory and final decisions on the size and timing of any deals have yet to be taken, they said, asking not to be identified because the discussions are private. A representative for Barclays declined to comment. Related: Insurer Rolls Out Policy to Protect Data Centers Against Growing Backlash Banks frequently use credit risk insurance to hedge portfolios, alongside derivatives, outright loan sales and significant risk transfers. By sharing the risk of losses with insurers or investors, lenders free up regulatory capital that can then be used to bid for more business. European Banks Want a Slice of AI Profits, But Less of the Risk As the AI-buildout accelerates, credit risk insurers have taken on greater exposure to data center finance, according to a survey from Willis Towers Watson Plc released in May. Still, there are signs that their capacity to underwrite much more may be drying up, given the sheer scale of demand. Several providers of so-called non-trade credit risk insurance had indicated that they were “approaching sector limits or are already full on data center exposure,” according to the Willis survey. With global spending on data centers projected by McKinsey & Co to hit $6.7 trillion by 2030, debt financing is expected to play a much bigger role. The strain is already starting to show. Wall Street’s AI Debt Machine Is Starting to Choke on Supply A measure of Meta Platforms Inc. credit risk hit a record high last week as plans to ramp up capital spending reignited fears of more debt issuance. Citadel’s co-chief investment officer, Pablo Salame, said Monday that the credit market is “getting jammed right now because it hasn’t figured out a good way” to offload risks linked to the borrowing binge. Barclays is looking for insurers to cover more than 50% of the credit risk on some of the AI-linked facilities, one of the people said. items.extracted_text: Avec 11,5 milliards d’euros de cotisations en août 2026, l’assurance vie demeure un levier essentiel pour financer l’économie française et européenne - France Assureurs À 11,5 milliards d’euros, les cotisations en assurance vie sont en baisse de −6 % en août 2026 par rapport au même mois de 2025. Les prestations du mois d’août 2026 s’élèvent à 9,5 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +15 % par rapport à août 2025. Elles atteignent ainsi leur plus haut niveau depuis trois ans pour un mois d’août. La collecte nette s’établit à +2,0 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −1,9 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle d’août 2025. Depuis le début de l’année, elle s’élève à +43,5 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +6,9 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. En août 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 11,5 milliards d’euros, en diminution de −6 % par rapport au même mois de 2025 où les cotisations avaient atteint un niveau exceptionnellement élevé (12,2 milliards d’euros, soit +27 % par rapport à août 2024). Les cotisations progressent de +3 % pour les supports en unités de compte (UC) mais diminuent pour les supports en euros (−10 %). Depuis début 2026, les cotisations atteignent 138,7 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +9,2 milliards d’euros, soit +7 % par rapport aux huit premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+10 %) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+5 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 37 % sur le mois d’août 2026 et se maintient à 40 % sur les huit premiers mois de l’année. À 9,5 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois d’août 2026 sont en hausse de +15 % par rapport à août 2025. Cette augmentation est portée essentiellement par les supports en UC (+27 %), tandis que ceux en euros enregistrent une hausse de +11 %. Les prestations atteignent ainsi leur plus haut niveau pour un mois d’août depuis trois ans, avec notamment 2,4 milliards d’euros de prestations sur les supports en UC. Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 95,2 milliards d’euros, en légère progression de +2,3 milliards d’euros, soit +2 % par rapport aux huit premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique concerne principalement les supports en UC qui augmentent de +1,5 milliard d’euros, tandis que les prestations des supports en euros sont en hausse de +0,8 milliard d’euros. La collecte nette s’établit donc à +2,0 milliards d’euros en août 2026. Les supports en UC représentent l’essentiel de cette dynamique, avec une collecte nette positive de +1,9 milliard d’euros, tandis que les supports en euros enregistrent une collecte positive de +0,2 milliard d’euros. Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +43,5 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +6,9 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. Les supports en UC concentrent une partie très majoritaire de cette collecte nette (+33,9 milliards d’euros), tandis que ceux en euros y contribuent à hauteur de +9,7 milliards d’euros. L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 171 milliards d’euros à fin août 2026, en hausse de +5,7 % sur un an (+117 milliards d’euros). Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : «En août 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie demeurent à un niveau élevé, à 11,5 milliards d’euros. Depuis le début de l’année, la dynamique de l’assurance vie confirme la confiance des Français dans ce produit d’épargne de long terme, qui leur permet de préparer leur avenir, tout en contribuant au financement de l’économie française. Avec 80 % de ses encours investis au sein de l’Union européenne et plus de la moitié sur le territoire français, l’assurance vie constitue un levier essentiel au service de la souveraineté nationale et européenne. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros. items.title: Ryan Specialty posts 4% organic growth for third quarter
items.original_title: Ryan Specialty posts 4% organic growth for third quarter
items.rss_title: Ryan Specialty posts 4% organic growth for third quarter
items.rss_description: Ryan Specialty reported 4% organic growth for the third quarter, in line with a slowdown predicted earlier in the year. But an executive predicted a modestly higher organic growth rate through the end of the year.
items.extracted_text: Turner (left) and Patrick G. Ryan Agents and Brokers , Financial Results Ryan Specialty Oct 29, 2026 Ryan Specialty reported 4% organic growth for the third quarter, in line with a slowdown predicted earlier in the year. But an executive predicted a modestly higher organic growth rate through the end of the year. “We delivered for shareholders in the face of a very challenging and evolving price environment,” said Patrick G. Ryan, founder and executive chairman. Executives said they expected property pricing to continue declining, while competition is increasing in high-hazard casualty lines. Organic revenue growth has slowed sharply over the year, down from 11.8% in the first quarter. The brokerage touted “new client wins, strong renewal retention, and expanded relationships with existing clients” despite the slowdown. Total revenue grew 4.7% year-over-year. Profits increased 40.6% from the prior-year quarter, or 4.1% on an adjusted basis. Mr. Ryan said the company had maintained margins despite the soft market. Adjusted earnings before net interest expense, income tax, depreciation, amortization and change in contingent consideration margin was 30.9% for the quarter, compared with 31.2% in the prior-year period. Chief Financial Officer Janice Hamilton predicted “higher end of mid-single digit organic growth” for 2026, while declining to make a prediction for next year. CEO Timothy W. Turner said property and casualty business was not migrating back into the admitted market. “It’s fierce competition in the non-admitted marketplace driving property prices down, and competition even in high-hazard casualty and spilling into the binding business as well, despite double-digit flow into the (excess and surplus) channel.” Mr. Turner said the brokerage was well positioned to profit from the rapid growth of data centers. In August, Ryan Specialty launched a new managing general underwriter, Tera Underwriters, and an accompanying specialty insurance program designed for computing hardware infrastructure at large data centers. Brokers must “scratch and claw” to build the “unprecedented” insurance towers for these massive projects, he said. items.extracted_text: Avec 15,4 milliards d’euros de cotisations en septembre 2026, les Français réaffirment leur confiance dans la solidité du modèle de l’assurance vie - France Assureurs En septembre 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 15,4 milliards d’euros, en progression de +2 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. À 11,3 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de septembre 2026 sont en hausse de +6 % par rapport à septembre 2025. La collecte nette s’établit à +4,1 milliards d’euros, en légère baisse par rapport à celle de septembre 2025 (+4,3 milliards d’euros). À 15,4 milliards d’euros, les cotisations atteignent leur plus haut niveau pour un mois de septembre En septembre 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 15,4 milliards d’euros, en progression de +2 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. Elles atteignent ainsi leur plus haut niveau pour un mois de septembre. La dynamique concerne essentiellement les supports en unités de compte (UC, +7 %), tandis que les supports en euros restent stables. Depuis le début de l’année, les cotisations atteignent 154,2 milliards d’euros, leur plus haut niveau sur les neuf premiers mois de l’année depuis 2006. Elles progressent de +9,5 milliards d’euros, soit +7 %, par rapport à la même période de 2025. Cette progression est portée à la fois par les supports en UC (+10 %) et par ceux en euros (+4 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 37 % sur le mois de septembre 2026 et à 39 % depuis le début de l’année. À 11,3 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de septembre 2026 sont en hausse de +6 % par rapport à septembre 2025. Cette augmentation concerne à la fois les supports en UC (+7 %) et les supports en euros (+5 %). Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 106,6 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +2,9 milliards d’euros, soit +3 % par rapport aux neuf premiers mois de 2025. Cette légère augmentation concerne à la fois les supports en UC (+1,7 milliard d’euros) et ceux en euros (+1,2 milliard d’euros). La collecte nette s’établit donc à +4,1 milliards d’euros en septembre 2026, en légère baisse de 0,3 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle du même mois de l’année précédente. Cette collecte nette positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+2,8 milliards d’euros) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+1,3 milliard d’euros). Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +47,6 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +6,7 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. Cette dynamique est principalement portée par les supports en UC (+36,7 milliards d’euros), suivis par les supports en euros (+10,9 milliards d’euros). L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 161 milliards d’euros à fin septembre 2026, en hausse de +4,6 % sur un an (+95 milliards d’euros). Au troisième trimestre 2026, les cotisations sur les PER assurantiels sont en hausse de +9 % Au troisième trimestre 2026, les cotisations (hors transferts) sur les PER assurantiels s’élèvent à 3,3 milliards d’euros, soit +9 % par rapport à la même période de 2025, pour 180 600 nouveaux PER souscrits. La collecte nette atteint +2,0 milliards d’euros, stable par rapport à la même période de 2025. Depuis le début de l’année 2026, les versements sur les PER assurantiels (y compris les transferts) s’élèvent à 13,3 milliards d’euros, en progression de +1 % par rapport à la même période en 2025. Les transferts d’anciens contrats d’épargne retraite vers les PER ont représenté 83 800 assurés pour un montant de 1,1 milliard d’euros au troisième trimestre 2026. À fin septembre 2026, les PER assurantiels comptabilisent 8,5 millions d’assurés pour un encours de 127,5 milliards d’euros. Les entreprises d’assurance représentaient 70 % de l’encours de l’ensemble des PER à fin décembre 2025. L’assurance vie, un modèle durable d’épargne de long terme au service de l’économie productive La complémentarité des supports en euros et en UC permet de répondre à l’ensemble des besoins des assurés, tout en finançant les entreprises et l’Etat sur le long terme. En effet, avec 64 % des encours de l’assurance vie investis dans le financement des entreprises (25 % en actions, 34 % en obligations d’entreprise et 6 % en immobilier d’entreprise) et 24 % des encours placés dans les obligations souveraines à fin décembre 2025, l’assurance vie mobilise l’épargne des Français pour le financement de l’économie productive. Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : « Avec 15,4 milliards de cotisations en septembre 2026, les Français réaffirment leur confiance dans l’assurance vie. La croissance soutenue des PER assurantiels depuis leur lancement fin 2019 témoigne de la solidité de ce produit d’épargne de long terme, dans un environnement économique et financier marqué par de fortes incertitudes. Grâce à la solidité du modèle assurantiel et grâce à la diversité des supports d’investissement, l’assurance vie accompagne les projets des Français dans la durée. Cet horizon d’investissement de long terme permet aux assureurs de répondre durablement aux besoins de financement des entreprises et de l’Etat, au-delà des fluctuations conjoncturelles des marchés. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros. items.extracted_text: Le Conseil constitutionnel abroge la mesure de gel des tarifs des complémentaires santé en 2026 - France Assureurs La Mutualité Française, la Fédération des Institutions paritaires de Protection Sociale et France Assureurs prennent acte de la décision du Conseil constitutionnel relative à l’article 13 de la loi de financement de la Sécurité sociale 2026. Cette décision confirme les réserves exprimées par les trois fédérations sur cette disposition, à la fois inapplicable, contraire à la Constitution et préjudiciable à la pérennité de la réponse aux besoins de protection des assurés sociaux. Dans un contexte de progression structurelle des dépenses de santé liée au vieillissement démographique, de transferts de charges et de hausse de la fiscalité décidés par les pouvoirs publics, le gel des tarifs aurait empêché les organismes de complémentaire santé de prendre les décisions économiques indispensables pour respecter leurs obligations envers leurs assurés sociaux. La décision du Conseil constitutionnel clarifie l’état du droit applicable et va donc permettre aux complémentaires santé de poursuivre sereinement leur engagement au service de la communauté des assurés sociaux. Les trois fédérations rappellent enfin leur volonté de poursuivre le dialogue avec les pouvoirs publics afin d’identifier des solutions structurelles pour la maîtrise de l’évolution des dépenses de santé et pour préserver l’accès aux soins de l’ensemble des Français. À propos de France Assureurs France Assureurs est le nom d’usage de la Fédération Française de l’Assurance qui rassemble 254 entreprises d’assurance et de réassurance représentant 99 % du marché des entreprises régies par le Code des assurances. L’assurance est au cœur des enjeux de société : à ce titre, France Assureurs a vocation à prendre une part active au débat public. Elle est l’interlocutrice privilégiée des pouvoirs publics, des administrations et des médias sur les sujets liés à l’assurance, en France et à l’international, qu’il s’agisse des questions de prévention, de protection, d’investissement ou d’emploi. Les données statistiques qu’elle centralise et son expertise lui permettent d’accompagner ses membres dans les évolutions du secteur. France Assureurs s’appuie sur un réseau de correspondants dans l’ensemble des territoires français pour accompagner les élus locaux en cas d’événement de grande ampleur ou pour valoriser les métiers de l’assurance ou encore pour relayer les positions du secteur. « Mobiliser toutes les énergies de l’assurance pour faire avancer la société en confiance » est la raison d’être de France Assureurs. France Assureurs – Faire avancer la société en confiance est une marque de la Fédération Française de l’Assurance. À propos de la FIPS La Fédération des institutions paritaires de protection sociale (FIPS) est l’organisation représentative des partenaires sociaux, et de l’ensemble des institutions de prévoyance et des groupes de protection sociale. Elle porte leur parole auprès des pouvoirs publics nationaux et européens. La FIPS représente les intérêts de 14 millions de salariés couverts dans plus de 2 millions d’entreprises. Avec ses 41 adhérents, elle développe une information pédagogique sur la protection sociale complémentaire et met en lumière l’efficacité du paritarisme de gestion pour concevoir et piloter des garanties adaptées aux besoins des salariés et de leurs proches en santé, prévoyance et retraite supplémentaire. Véritable force de proposition, elle agit sur l’ensemble du champ de la protection sociale complémentaire, avec la conviction que celle-ci contribue à la compétitivité et à l’attractivité des entreprises au bénéfice des salariés. À propos de la Mutualité Française Acteur majeur de l’économie sociale et solidaire, la Mutualité Française, présidée par Eric Chenut, représente près de 500 mutuelles. Nées de la volonté de femmes et d’hommes de se protéger solidairement des aléas de la vie, les mutuelles sont des sociétés de personnes à but non lucratif. Elles sont présidées par des militants mutualistes élus. Elles agissent pour la protection sociale de 32 millions de Français et promeuvent le droit de tous à la pleine santé en intervenant en complémentarité et en partenariat avec la Sécurité Sociale et en contribuant au service public de santé. Les mutuelles, groupes et unions proposent des solutions dans trois domaines d’activités : complémentaire santé, prévoyance-dépendance et épargne-retraite. Avec plus de 2900 services de soins et d’accompagnement mutualistes, elles jouent un rôle majeur pour l’accès aux soins, dans les territoires, à un tarif maîtrisé. Elles sont aussi le 1er acteur privé de prévention en santé par les actions déployées sur l’ensemble du territoire. Au quotidien, les membres de la Mutualité Française déclinent autour de trois territoires d’engagement – proximité, participation et innovation – sa raison d’être : “Se protéger mutuellement aujourd’hui pour, ensemble, construire les solidarités de demain”. items.extracted_text: Violences urbaines : les assureurs se mobilisent pour accompagner leurs assurés et accélérer l’indemnisation - France Assureurs Les assureurs sont pleinement mobilisés pour accompagner les particuliers, les commerçants, les entreprises et les collectivités territoriales dont les biens ont été endommagés ou détruits. La cellule de crise de France Assureurs agit en lien étroit avec les pouvoirs publics dans les territoires concernés. Les assureurs s’engagent à : porter à 30 jours le délai de déclaration de sinistre, généralement fixé à 5 jours ouvrés dans les contrats d’assurance accélérer l’indemnisation, en lien étroit avec les cabinets d’expertise, afin d’organiser rapidement les visites et de traiter en priorité les situations les plus sensibles faciliter le versement d’acomptes pour faire face aux situations les plus difficiles. Le 17 octobre 2026, plusieurs villes françaises ont connu des violences urbaines et des pillages. France Assureurs et ses membres expriment leur soutien à toutes les personnes touchées par ces violences. Les assureurs sont pleinement mobilisés pour accompagner les particuliers, les commerçants, les entreprises et les collectivités territoriales dont les biens ont été endommagés. La cellule de crise de France Assureurs agit en lien étroit avec les pouvoirs publics dans les territoires concernés. La Fédération recommande à chaque assuré d’effectuer rapidement un dépôt de plainte puis une déclaration de sinistre. Cette dernière peut être effectuée par l’ensemble des moyens de contact mis à disposition par son assureur (courrier postal, email, téléphone, sms, etc.). Dans ces circonstances exceptionnelles, les assureurs s’engagent à : porter à 30 jours le délai de déclaration de sinistre, généralement fixé à 5 jours dans les contrats d’assurance accélérer l’indemnisation, en lien étroit avec les cabinets d’expertise, afin d’organiser rapidement les visites et de traiter en priorité les situations les plus sensibles faciliter le versement d’acomptes pour faire face aux situations les plus difficiles. Pour plus d’informations sur les garanties et les couvertures, cliquez ici Florence Lustman, présidente de France Assureurs , déclare : « Les violences urbaines qui ont eu lieu dans notre pays le 17 octobre dernier affectent profondément nos concitoyens. Au nom de l’ensemble des assureurs, je tiens à exprimer notre solidarité et notre soutien à toutes les personnes qui subissent les conséquences de ces événements d’une violence exceptionnelle. Les assureurs sont pleinement mobilisés pour accompagner leurs assurés et leur apporter des réponses concrètes. Les mesures annoncées aujourd’hui témoignent de l’engagement collectif de la profession pour simplifier et accélérer l’indemnisation. » Document à télécharger Communiqué de presse – Violences urbaines items.extracted_text: L’emploi dans l’assurance en 2025 : publication des données clés - France Assureurs L’ Observatoire de l’évolution des métiers de l’assurance (OEMA) publie son 30e rapport sur les métiers et les formations des salariés de l’assurance. Les effectifs continuent de progresser malgré un contexte incertain. L’emploi pérenne et l’investissement dans la formation restent des points forts de la branche. Retrouvez les principaux enseignements du ROMA 2026. Des effectifs toujours en hausse, portés par l’emploi pérenne Au 31 décembre 2025, la branche des sociétés d’assurances compte 162 700 salariés, soit une progression de 0,9 % en un an. Plus modérée que les années précédentes, cette croissance témoigne toutefois de la solidité de l’emploi dans l’assurance. La branche confirme également sa préférence pour l’emploi durable : 93,6 % des salariés sont en CDI, une proportion qui atteint son plus haut niveau depuis 2017. Des recrutements toujours supérieurs au nombre de départs en 2025 Les sociétés d’assurances ont recruté 18 400 personnes en 2025. Les nouveaux entrants représentent 11,3 % des effectifs. 15,5% des salariés ont connu une mobilité en 2025, moins 2,2 points par rapport à 2024. La répartition des mobilités est fortement dépendante du domaine de métier. A l’instar des années passées, les femmes sont plus nombreuses à bénéficier de mobilités internes (61,7 % vs 38,8 % pour les hommes). Le taux de turnover se stabilise quant à lui à 7 %, retrouvant son niveau d’avant la crise sanitaire. Des emplois de plus en plus qualifiés et un encadrement qui se féminise Les cadres représentent désormais 54 % des salariés de la branche, contre 46 % en 2015. Cette progression reflète la montée en qualification des emplois, portée notamment par les transformations technologiques du secteur. L’alternance conserve une place importante malgré une légère baisse Avec 7 200 alternants en poste au 31 décembre 2025, les alternants représentent 4,4% des effectifs de la branche, en légère baisse par rapport à l’année passée. Une baisse par ailleurs inférieure à celle constatée au niveau national, estimée à 5% du nombre de contrats d’apprentissage. L’alternance demeure néanmoins une voie privilégiée d’entrée dans les métiers de l’assurance : 4 500 alternants ont été recrutés en 2025, soit près d’un quart des embauches de la branche. Les formations préparées sont majoritairement ancrées dans l’enseignement supérieur : 53,6 % des alternants visent un diplôme de niveau bac +5 ou plus. Les sociétés d’assurances continuent aussi d’accueillir des jeunes titulaires d’un diplôme de niveau bac ou inférieur, contribuant à leur professionnalisation. Près de neuf salariés sur dix ont bénéficié d’une formation La formation continue reste un engagement fort des sociétés d’assurances. En 2025, 145 600 salariés ont suivi au moins une formation, soit 89,5 % des effectifs, pour une durée moyenne de 33,3 heures par salarié formé. Cet investissement concerne toutes les catégories de salariés. Le taux d’accès à la formation ainsi que le nombre d’heures de formation suivi sont très corrélés au domaine de métier et aux fonctions occupées. Ainsi, les métiers de la distribution et du développement commercial comptabilisent un nombre d’heures de formation moyen annuel, supérieur à la moyenne de la branche avec 50,2 heures (vs 33.3 heures). L’Observatoire de l’évolution des métiers de l’assurance L’Observatoire a pour mission d’informer la profession sur les facteurs susceptibles de faire évoluer les métiers. Ses travaux doivent permettre aux acteurs concernés d’en tirer les conséquences en termes de qualifications, ou encore de besoins de formation. Par ses éclairages, il participe à la gestion prévisionnelle des emplois et des compétences. Les travaux de l’Observatoire sont mis à la disposition des sociétés d’assurances, des organisations d’employeurs et de salariés, des étudiants, ainsi que des organismes professionnels intervenant dans les domaines de l’emploi, de la formation et de l’enseignement… Publié chaque année, le Rapport de l’Observatoire sur les Métiers et les formations de l’Assurance (ROMA) consolide les données socioprofessionnelles de l’ensemble des adhérents de France Assureurs. items.extracted_text: LCB-FT : un guide pour connaître les informations, justificatifs et données personnelles que votre professionnel de l’assurance peut vous demander - France Assureurs Les professionnels du secteur financier (banques, assurances…) participent à la lutte contre le blanchiment d’argent et le financement du terrorisme (LCB-FT), notamment parce qu’ils gèrent des produits d’épargne sur lesquels pourraient être versés des fonds issus ou destinés à ces activités illégales. La réglementation relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme (LCB-FT) leur impose de mettre en œuvre des mesures de vigilance. Ils doivent notamment vérifier l’identité de leurs clients, connaître leur situation et exercer un contrôle sur leurs opérations afin d’identifier celles qui pourraient présenter un risque. Concrètement, votre assureur peut être amené à vous demander des informations sur votre situation personnelle et professionnelle, votre patrimoine ou encore vos revenus. Il peut également vous interroger sur l’origine des fonds versés sur un contrat d’assurance vie, ainsi que sur la destination ou l’utilisation des sommes versées lors du dénouement de ce contrat par exemple. Ce guide, réalisé par AGEA, France Assureurs et Planète CSCA, a pour objectif d’expliquer aux assurés les raisons pour lesquelles les professionnels de l’assurance leur demandent des informations, justificatifs et données personnelles. items.extracted_text: Nouvel épisode d’Assurément Margaux – Assurance scolaire : obligatoire… ou pas ? - France Assureurs Alors que son week-end à Noirmoutier prend un tournant inattendu, Margaux fait la connaissance de Carole, la sœur de Simon. Très vite, tandis que Margaux pense encore à ses histoires de cœur, Carole, elle, ne parle que de son fils… et de sa récente blessure à l’école. Curieuse comme à son habitude, Margaux se laisse finalement embarquer dans le sujet et découvre que l’assurance scolaire ne se résume pas aux salles de classe. Selon les situations, elle peut aussi couvrir les dommages causés à un autre élève, certaines activités périscolaires ou encore inclure des garanties utiles pendant la convalescence de l’enfant. De quoi rassurer les parents… bien au-delà de la cour de récréation. L’assurance scolaire est-elle obligatoire ? Que couvre-t-elle en cas d’accident ? Comment choisir une couverture adaptée aux activités de son enfant ? Un épisode qui répond aux questions que beaucoup de parents se posent… souvent le jour où un imprévu survient. items.extracted_text: Avec 18,8 milliards d’euros de cotisations en juillet 2026, l’assurance vie maintient son cap au service du financement de l’économie - France Assureurs En juillet 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 18,8 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +1 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. À 14,1 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juillet 2026 sont en hausse de +4 % par rapport à juillet 2025. La collecte nette s’établit à +4,7 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −0,4 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle de juillet 2025. En juillet 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 18,8 milliards d’euros, en légère augmentation de +1 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. Elles dépassent ainsi le précédent record établi sur la même période l’an dernier (18,7 milliards d’euros). Les cotisations progressent pour les supports en unités de compte (UC, +5 %), cette dynamique étant en partie compensée par une baisse sur les supports en euros (−2%). Depuis début 2026, les cotisations atteignent 127,8 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +10,4 milliards d’euros, soit +9 % par rapport aux sept premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+11 %) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+8 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 42 % sur le mois de juillet 2026 et à 40 % sur les sept premiers mois de l’année. À 14,1 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juillet 2026 sont en hausse de +4 % par rapport à juillet 2025. Cette augmentation est portée essentiellement par les supports en UC (+8 %), tandis que ceux en euros enregistrent une hausse plus modérée (+2 %). Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 86,5 milliards d’euros, en légère progression de +1,8 milliard d’euros, soit +2 % par rapport aux sept premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique concerne principalement les supports en UC (+1,6 milliard d’euros), tandis que les prestations des supports en euros restent quasiment stables (+0,2 milliard d’euros). La collecte nette s’établit donc à +4,7 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −0,4 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle du même mois de l’année précédente. Les supports en euros enregistrent une collecte positive de +0,9 milliard d’euros et les supports en UC poursuivent également leur dynamique haussière (+3,8 milliards d’euros). Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +41,3 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +8,7 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. Les supports en UC concentrent l’essentiel de cette collecte nette (+31,3 milliards d’euros), tandis ceux en euros y contribuent dans une moindre mesure (+10,0 milliards d’euros). L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 174 milliards d’euros à fin juillet 2026, en hausse de +6,3 % sur un an (+128 milliards d’euros). Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : « Avec un record de 18,8 milliards d’euros de cotisations en juillet, l’assurance vie confirme une nouvelle fois sa solidité et son attractivité auprès des Français. Cette dynamique illustre son rôle majeur dans leur épargne de long terme, mais aussi dans le financement de l’économie. Préserver pleinement cette contribution essentielle au financement de l’économie française et européenne constitue un enjeu majeur. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros.
